notes: §1985:XIV.3.6.3 SR2: "Identifier-2 must reference a one-character integer without an operational sign." CommunicationBinder#BindSend refuses (COBOL6171, quoting the 1985 rule at --std 85) an operand IsIntegerItem rejects. IsIntegerItem judges the operand as bound (kb/Work PB5384): a data item asks the one integer classifier IntrinsicResultType#IsIntegerOperand, which answers false for a reference-modified operand (a numeric item's slice is class and category alphanumeric, §1985:IV.4.3.8.4.4 GR5), and then the one-digit unsigned test of its PICTURE (P is not counted, §1985:VI.5.9.4 GR8); a LINAGE-COUNTER is asked through its implicit description (AlgebraicRanges#CounterRegisterDescription), whose size is the page size's (§1985:VII.1.3.7), so the counter of LINAGE IS 9 passes and of LINAGE IS 60 is refused; every other computed operand (a function, an index-name) is refused. Probes at --std 85 on this tree: I9 (1:1) and LINAGE-COUNTER of LINAGE IS 60 refused COBOL6171; LINAGE-COUNTER of LINAGE IS 9 accepted and sent ESI (end key 1); PIC 9, 9P accepted as before; 99 refused.

next.reason: 1985: "Identifier-2 must reference a one-character integer without an operational sign."; 2023: "2023 SEND is the message-server SEND (message-server-name-1, message-tag data items); it has no end-indicator identifier-2.". The communication module's SEND and its end-indicator identifier-2 are gone. The 2023 SEND rules cover message servers only, and no candidate restates the one-character unsigned integer rule.
